entries.title: We’re announcing Genie 4, our new world model for real-time interactive simulation.
entries.summary: Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation.The Genie 4 m…
entries.content:
Today, we’re announcing our research on Genie 4, our new world model that brings unprecedented realism and native audio to real-time interactive simulation.

The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity.

With Genie 4, you can set an event in motion and steer scenes in real time using natural language, like moving the camera, changing the weather, or introducing new characters. Every world also generates native audio on the fly, including ambient sounds, music, and interactive dialogue.

Simulating the world is a crucial step toward AGI, enabling safe training environments for robots and agents, and amplifying creative tools across industries like filmmaking, journalism, gaming, and manufacturing.

We have started rolling out Genie 4 to a limited group of trusted testers. It’s coming soon to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and early access partners in the Gemini API and AI Studio.

Explore the demos on the Google DeepMind blog.

entries.title: 8 examples of Gemini 4 Argon in action
entries.summary: Collage of various uses of Gemini 4 Argon
entries.content:
Our newest model, Gemini 4 Argon, was built to solve your hardest problems. By tackling complex, real-world tasks and taking on high-stakes work that used to require months of manual effort, it's fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google — and it can do the same for you. Go ahead and hand over dense research materials, raw photos, and multi-step projects. Argon will reason, code, and coordinate tools to deliver what you need.

From deep research to interactive 3D design, here are eight examples of what our most intelligent model yet can do.

Handling complex tasks

Using advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities, Gemini 4 Argon excels in deep comprehension and long-horizon workflows. From a short prompt and with zero assets or libraries, Argon wrote 5,000 lines of math to render a 3D sunlit library from scratch — and then made a video about the process.

Making interactive tools and playable 3D games

Googlers have used Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations. When prompted to build an app to overlay shapes across videos, Gemini 4 Argon in the Gemini app generated a custom audiovisual tool that traces musical scale lines from frame to frame. The motion of the video triggers musical notes, creating a dynamic audio composition.

To turn your world into an interactive game, start with photos of a physical space and our AI Studio how-to. We used Argon in Antigravity to orchestrate subagents, Blender MCP, and Nano Banana to transform pictures of a real desk into a playable 3D track.

Optimizing workflows

Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities to help with high-stakes professional workflows. Given a custom slides template and more than 80,000 raw files from NASA — including weather logs and engineering, health, and science data accumulated across 72 flights on Mars — Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity was able to parse information, organize insights, and turn it all into an executive-ready deck with clear visual narratives.

Building engaging visuals

Gemini 4 Argon is especially strong when work requires visual understanding. When prompted to make dense academic chapters come alive, Argon used Nano Banana and Veo to transform the scientific concepts in a PDF into an illustrated animation of key moments in the Gemini app.

To create an unforgettable science explainer in Antigravity, Argon generated a self-navigating 3D periodic table with animated atoms choreographed with frame-accurate audio timing to the rapid-fire lyrics of “The Elements” by Tom Lehrer.

Generating lifelike textures

Argon brings a deeper understanding of real-time 3D rendering, lighting and shading, and interactive physics simulation. This allows Argon in Antigravity to code a custom “fur engine” with studio-grade hair dynamics, generating visually rich fur that grows and moves as a character does.

We also used Argon in Antigravity to create an interactive musical “G” with fluid physics and reactive sound.

Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

entries.title: Fitbit Edge: Premium design for an active life
entries.content:
When we set out to design the new Fitbit Edge, 1 we asked ourselves a fundamental question: How do we reimagine the fitness tracker to establish a bold new standard for performance, aesthetics, and comfort?

For millions of people, a lightweight, discreet tracker is the ideal health and fitness companion. But active lifestyles demand more than just passive tracking. They require at-a-glance readability, dependable durability, and all-day comfort. With Fitbit Edge, we reconsidered every curve, interaction, and material to create a wearable device that feels as natural during a strenuous workout as it does at a dinner party.

Instant glanceability

Our first major design focus was the screen. When you’re mid-stride during a run, you shouldn’t have to squint or break your rhythm to check your stats.

Our largest, brightest tracker display yet features a brilliant Hybrid OLED panel that’s easy to read, even with a harsh outdoor glare. 2 We paired the screen with a completely overhauled UX and UI, structuring information into glanceable, high-contrast tiles and expressive clock faces that spotlight your key health and fitness information while delivering a distinctive look that elevates Fitbit Edge’s unique form.

Precision control and fit

We carefully designed the mechanical architecture to include a tactile physical side button. A responsive touchscreen is great for daily navigation, but when you're mid-workout, tactility is everything. Sweaty fingers or wet weather can make on-screen tapping frustrating, but the ergonomic side button ensures that pausing your workout — or taking any other quick actions — is just a click away.

To ensure Fitbit Edge fits well, we sculpted the thin chassis and bottom sensor housing with a subtle curve. By contouring the device to match the anatomy of your wrist, we minimized pressure points while ensuring continuous skin contact for 24/7 heart-rate and sleep tracking.

Enduring design

Water- and dust-resistant, 3 Fitbit Edge balances elegance with active durability. Its chassis is made from 100% recycled aluminum 4 and comes in four finishes: Obsidian, Olive, Canyon, and Fog.

Our accessories have also been completely redesigned. 5 Switching up your look is easy whether you opt for a sleek, minimalist look or an active, athletic design.

  • Active Sport Band: Features wide perforations for maximum breathability during intense workouts. Available in Obsidian, Porcelain, Olive, and Hibiscus.
  • Performance Loop Band: 6 Combines stretchable, micro-adjustable fabric with custom swivel lugs to wrap closely to your wrist. Available in Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon.
  • Magnet Band: Pairs a premium silicone substrate with soft magnets for an intuitive clasp and a clean, minimalist silhouette. Available in Obsidian, Fog, and Mahogany.
  • Metal Link Band: Brings a classic, refined aesthetic to your daily companion. Available in Matte Black, Brushed Silver, and Champagne Gold.

When you're wearing a device 24/7, you need to trust that it's built to last. We thoughtfully crafted every detail of Fitbit Edge to stand up to your toughest days and keep up with your active lifestyle. With up to seven days of battery life, 7 it lets you spend less time plugged in and more time getting after your goals.

entries.title: 15 college students share their favorite Gemini features
entries.summary: Three young adults gathered around a laptop looking at its screen
entries.content:
College students have found all kinds of ways to use Gemini. It helps them learn better, track workouts, turn groceries into tasty meals, vibe-code portfolios — and then review them from a hiring manager’s point of view.

So we asked 15 Google Student Ambassadors to share their favorite Gemini features — and how they use them to study smarter, learn faster, produce better work, and stay organized.

1. Study notebooks

Study notebooks turn your course materials into personalized, bite-sized lessons. “They make studying more manageable, especially right before finals when I have a semester’s worth of material to review,” says Beverlyn T., University of Southern California.

Students use study notebooks for everything from organizing daily coursework to finding themes within their notes. “Study notebooks have made refreshing my memory on 50-page papers before class so much faster,” says Nina R., University of California, Santa Barbara. “And if you upload competing viewpoints, you can quickly generate comparisons and master complex concepts.

2. Gemini Live

Gemini Live lets you chat with Gemini using just your voice. “It’s my go-to for practicing interviews and presentations, because it lets me hear how my ideas actually sound,” says Skylar E., San Diego State University. Other students use it to talk through tough concepts on-the-go or practice speaking new languages before studying abroad.

You can also turn on your camera to show Gemini Live exactly what you’re looking at. “As a designer, I’m constantly learning new tools and software,” says Debbie C., The University of Texas, Austin. “When I get stuck using one, I can have Gemini Live walk me through it step-by-step.”

3. Guided Learning

Guided Learning helps you build understanding instead of just giving you answers. “I paste in my work, and instead of asking for the fix, I let Gemini walk me toward what went wrong,” says Fehmaan K., George Mason University. “It asks me what I think happens at each step, and I usually catch my mistake before it tells me.”

Guided Learning asks open-ended questions to probe your understanding. “Resist asking for the answer when you get stuck mid-session,” Fehmaan adds. “Guess even when you’re unsure. Because getting corrected will stick with you more than reading an explanation.”

4. Study guides

Gemini can turn your notes into ready-made study guides. “For courses where professors don’t provide exam overviews, this helps me review content and summarize what I need to know,” says Jamie C., University of Southern California.

You can upload course materials, like lecture slides or handwritten notes, and tell Gemini what to include. “I recommend dedicating a Google Drive folder to each class you’re taking and sharing that with Gemini,” Jamie adds. “That way, your study guide captures both the professor’s content and your interpretations.”

5. Quizzes

Want to check how well you understand a subject? Gemini can generate custom quizzes to help you prep for tests and exams. “Practice quizzes help me build confidence going into high-stakes tests,” says Shuang P., New York University. “Many of my grades depend entirely on exams, so having access to extra practice questions is critical.”

When teachers provide practice tests without answer keys, some students use Gemini quizzes to check their work — and understand the logic behind each question. “It helps understand what questions I might miss or misinterpret,” says Tobi U., University of California, Riverside.

6. Unlimited uploads

Gemini student plans give you unlimited uploads of class materials, study notebooks, interactive visualizations, and images in general. “This really helps me provide context in my notes,” says Chaeyeon H., Boston University. Say you want to reference something like a homework assignment, lecture slide, historic artifact, or work of art. “Whether it’s a physical object or something on my screen, I can easily snap and upload a photo,” says Nicole F., University of California, San Diego.

Other students use the feature before submitting work, uploading their draft and the assignment rubric to double-check that they’ve met every requirement.

7. Audio Overviews

With Audio Overviews, you can create podcast-style conversations from documents, slides, and more. “I rely on Audio Overviews to get in last-minute review sessions while walking across campus,” Nina says. “This lets me absorb things conversationally and take active notes while listening.”

Students say Audio Overviews are especially handy for more thoroughly exploring class materials and topics. “I like to upload articles with conflicting viewpoints. The hosts naturally argue both sides of the issue,” says Parikshit M., Rutgers University.

8. Image generation

Nano Banana, Gemini’s image generator, can help you visualize any idea and design anything. “As a creative, I’ve found image generation models helpful, especially when formatting images and sharpening details,” says Nelson G., Morehouse College.

Students are using it outside the classroom, too. “I often get overwhelmed when designing graphics,” Beverlyn says. “I love using Gemini to create club flyers and social media posts. It turns my ideas into eye-catching visuals tailored closely to my style.”

9. Gemini in Chrome

With Gemini in Chrome, you can get assistance directly in your browser. “It makes reviewing wrong answers on exams so much more efficient, because I don’t have to copy and paste them into a Gemini chat,” says Megan J., University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

It’s also great for deciphering complex documents. “I can get context without opening a new tab and losing my place,” Fehmaan says. “I recommend using it for ‘What does this specific sentence mean?’ — the narrow questions are where it saves the most time.”

10. Deep Research

Deep Research can automatically browse up to hundreds of websites, think through its findings, and create multi-page reports in minutes. Plus, you can talk through the findings on the go with Gemini Live.

“It saves me so much time by compiling exhaustive market analyses and literature reviews,” says Annitha K., San Diego State University. “I like to use Gemini to brainstorm a tightly structured research prompt and then feed that into Deep Research.”

11. Connected apps

Connecting Gemini to other apps — like Google Drive, Google Calendar, Gmail, and Google Sheets — can help you stay organized. “I have Gemini reference class syllabi in my Drive, find every assignment and due date, and organize them in my Calendar,” Skylar says. “Before winding down, I have Gemini log all my tasks in a master tracking Sheet so I start each morning organized,” says Aaryaman B., Michigan State University.

It can also help you stave off inbox chaos. “As a TA for a class, I never want emails from my students to get lost,” Megan says. “Gemini helps me find messages I need to respond to or follow up on, saving time and helping me be a more present educator.”

entries.title: Our newest AI Quest: Mapping the human brain
entries.summary: An illustration of a planet rotating to show various cartoon figures waving. At the top is the text "AI Quests"
entries.content:
Today, we’re launching “Polar Peaks”, our third quest in the AI Quests series, created by Google Research and the Stanford Accelerator for Learning to teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly. AI Quests invites students ages 11 to 14 to step into the shoes of Google researchers to tackle some of humanity’s biggest challenges.

More than 400,000 quests have been completed to date, localized to 10 languages. Alongside the new quest, we’re also releasing training modules for teachers.

Polar Peaks: A journey to map the human brain

In the first two quests, students tackle flood forecasting and eye disease detection, inspired by Google Research’s Flood Forecasting initiative and AI model for diabetic retinopathy screening. Our newest quest, “Polar Peaks,” has students travel to the frontiers of neuroscience and see how AI can speed up scientific research.

With the guidance of in-game mentors, students scan and map the neurons in the brain to better understand the game character’s memory loss. They complete tasks like data cleaning and model testing, learning firsthand that AI requires careful human oversight and critical thinking.

The quest is inspired by over a decade of our research in connectomics: the science of mapping neural networks in the brain. Upon completion of the quest, students hear from two researchers behind our real-world breakthroughs, including the recent mapping of the complete fruit fly brain, the largest brain map by number of neurons to date.

Training modules: Tools for teaching AI literacy

Teachers play a critical role in bringing the quests to life and fitting them into their existing classroom curriculum. We’re rolling out new dedicated teacher training modules to help educators reinforce key AI literacy concepts and use AI Quests for learning and discussion. These are launching within the Google AI Educator Series. The modules for Quest #1 and #2 are accessible here. The training module for Quest #3 will follow next month.

Earlier this year, AI Quests won a 2026 Webby Award for AI Education, Learning & Training, and Best Global K–12 Learning Solution at the ETIH Innovation Awards. We’ll continue working with educators and partners to bring more quests to more classrooms this school year.

entries.title: Powering sub-Saharan Africa beyond the grid
entries.summary: A person holding up a solar panel
entries.content:
Across sub-Saharan Africa, nearly half the continent’s population — over 600 million people — live without electricity. Families rely on costly kerosene and candles for basic lighting to study, do chores, or move safely around the home.

Off-grid solar power offers one of the cleanest and fastest ways to bridge this gap.

In order to reach millions of dispersed households with this technology, we must solve three critical challenges: locating unmapped homes without formal addresses, navigating difficult rural terrain to deliver solar hardware, and identifying installations remotely despite the limits of satellite imagery.

To help on-the-ground climate innovators solve data and logistical barriers beyond our own operational footprint, Google spent the past three years collaborating with Ignite Energy Access through our Startups for Sustainable Development program. An off-grid clean energy pioneer aiming to connect 100 million people throughout Africa to electricity by 2030 Ignite worked alongside Google researchers, engineers, and data specialists across more than 100 dedicated advisory sessions,to transform these logistical roadblocks into a repeatable blueprint for expanding energy access.

Solving last-mile logistics

Most rural communities are only connected by unmapped dirt paths across rugged terrain. To expand access to off-grid solar, the first step is pinpointing households that need it, and these homes don’t appear in standard mapping apps. To locate these, our joint team combined satellite imagery and Google’s Open Buildings dataset with smart routing algorithms.

The field teams then need to reach these remote households. Google researchers are developing advanced geospatial models that identify rural paths and incorporate them into real-world routing constraints.

Google's Operations Research (OR) models are helping to optimize Ignite’s end-to-end supply chain. By evaluating potential network configurations, the system identifies where central warehouses and local mini-hubs should go while carefully balancing operational constraints such as transportation costs, delivery routes, vehicle capacities, and inventory holding expenses.

Scaling electrification from space

As electrification ramps up across Africa, operators need to know where micro-solar systems (usually consisting of a single rooftop panel) are already active. Mapping these installations allows teams to identify underserved villages, deploy resources strategically, and plan future rollouts.

However, standard satellite imagery only registers a single rooftop panel as barely one pixel, so visual targeting is nearly impossible at scale.

To solve this, Google researchers are developing computer vision models using Gemini for Science and fine-tuning them with ground-truth drone imagery provided by Ignite to map solar setups from orbit. The team is testing thousands of code variations to increase precision and recall rates, turning satellite data into a strategic compass for future clean-energy deployment.

Transforming local economies

Together, what began as a set of isolated friction points — unmapped dirt paths and single-pixel satellite signatures — is evolving into a playbook for expanding energy access while cutting emissions in emerging markets worldwide.

The environmental impact is already measurable: In the first half of 2026 alone, we estimate our partnership with Ignite Energy Access has enabled over 160,000 tCO2e in emissions reductions, driven by 3.7 million solar devices delivered across the region since 2023. 1 These milestones bring us closer to Google’s aspiration to help partners collectively reduce one gigaton of carbon-equivalent emissions annually by 2030.

Laying the groundwork

Google and Ignite are already preparing for the next phase in the energy transition: clean cooking.

Millions of rural families still rely on wood and charcoal for meals, filling homes with harmful smoke and requiring hours of daily fuel collection, a burden disproportionately affecting women and girls. Modern electric cookstoves eliminate these indoor toxins, but they require far more power than what an individual rooftop solar kit can generate.

To address this challenge, our partnership is modeling community-level micro-grids capable of delivering the energy required to power clean electric cooking. The goal is a comprehensive energy system that not only lights rural homes, but also protects family health and drives down household emissions.

Are you a founder or developer building technology for climate action? Explore how you can collaborate with us through the Startups for Sustainable Development program or access open-source resources like the Open Buildings dataset.

entries.title: We’re helping farmers around the world connect to essential services online.
entries.summary: Google.org is investing $2.5M to help 1 million farmers access AI-powered agricultural services via the World Bank's ONA. See how it works.
entries.content:
Under the World Bank Group’s AgriConnect initiative, Google.org is supporting the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and broader World Bank Group (WBG) to better empower farmers .

Their collective goal is to help 1 million farmers access crucial livelihood-improving services by the end of 2027. With Google.org’s $2.5 million in support, the WBG will expand digital public infrastructure (DPI) for agriculture: shared digital systems that act as “public roads” for online services.

Following a successful pilot in India, the WBG will build an AI-enabled Open Network for Agriculture (ONA) across several countries spanning Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa. By connecting public and private sector service providers in a shared digital network, ONA lets farmers avoid separate, disconnected apps, using a single platform to access vital resources like digital farmer IDs, credit lines, direct subsidy payments, markets to sell produce, and voice-powered advice in their local language on farming, weather, pricing, and finances.

This support builds on an alliance between Google and the World Bank Group to accelerate digital transformation in emerging markets.

entries.title: How Google Beam connects military families globally
entries.summary: Several military families communicating with Google Beam
entries.content:
For deployed service members, the hardest distance is measured in missed moments. A child’s first steps, a first performance, or simply sitting across the table from a loved one feels out of reach.

That's why we’re partnering with the USO to bring HP Dimension with Google Beam to 20 USO locations globally, helping service members bridge this distance. With Beam’s unique true-to-life, 3D video communication experience, families feel like they’re stepping into the same room and connecting in a whole new way.

Google Beam began a pilot program connecting families between Trzebień, Poland, and Fort Bliss, Texas earlier this year. Now, we’re releasing a docuseries that shows how the program is expanding to Grafenwöhr, Germany, and Fort Hood, Texas, bringing this lifelike closeness to even more families.

Directed by military veteran and filmmaker Kyle Hausmann-Stokes, our new docuseries captures the power of this connection. It follows four soldiers from the 2nd Battalion, 37th Armored Regiment (Iron Dukes) during their deployment in Poland. Watch the profound emotional impact of Google Beam as they reconnect with their families back home, proving that love knows no distance.

Four families, one shared mission

The Brown-Orane family

Sergeant Amoy Brown is a Bradley Gunner deployed in Poland, and Tiyanna Orane, his wife, is an aviation logistics specialist in Fort Bliss. For them, military service is an equal partnership. But an eight-hour time difference makes celebrating major milestones,like Tiyanna’s military promotion, feel distant. Google Beam helped create an intimate, lifelike reunion where Amoy and Tiyanna could celebrate her achievement, and Amoy could interact with their young son, Azeal.

The Kassales family

Throughout his first two years of service, Army Chaplain Roland Kassales has been deployed for 15 months. Staying present with this family during the time apart is incredibly important. Google Beam helped bridge the distance, bringing his family into focus. When his daughter, Blythe, read stories she wrote to him aloud, Beam let him experience those moments in real time with the body language, eye contact, and all.

The Jennings family

Mayra Jennings manages a bustling, blended household of seven while working 12-hour work shifts, leaving her deployed husband, Sergeant First Class Matthew Jennings, feeling the absence of daily family life. Standard phone calls made it difficult to connect across the miles with their 4-year-old son, Dimitri, their newborn daughter, Lilly, and his two sisters. Google Beam gave Matthew a front-row seat to experience how much his newborn daughter had grown, to see one of his sisters play guitar, and offered Mayra a moment of comfort, recreating the feeling and warmth of sitting directly across the table from one another.

The Rodriguez family

Major Michael Rodriguez, an armor battalion operations officer with 12 years of service, knows the heavy toll deployments take, especially on his family. His wife Jessica balances a demanding job as a pediatric physical therapist, while solo parenting their four young children. With Google Beam they’re able to create new memories, including witnessing his one-year-old daughter Kathryn practice taking her first steps.

Watch the docuseries

To see these emotional reunions and follow the journey of the Brown, Kassales, Jennings, and Rodriguez families, watch the complete docuseries. And to learn more about how Beam is redefining human connection visit goo.gle/USO.

entries.title: See what 5 builders are making with Gemini 4 Argon
entries.summary: Collage showing five builds with Gemini 4 Argon
entries.content:
Gemini 4 Argon, our new frontier model, excels at tackling complex projects. Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks to help across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains.

Since we rolled out Argon broadly last week, we've seen builders tap into its expanded abilities to create interactive tools, engineer 3D worlds, and more. These five builds from the community — including a globe that maps tectonic shockwaves in real time and a 3D multiplayer game — are some of our favorites so far.

Simulate a seaplane on water.

With major upgrades in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding, Gemini 4 Argon can generate complex 3D environments. In this test by Lumina (@LuminaBench on X), Argon rendered a 3D simulation of a seaplane with realistic lighting, reflections, and water movement. Because Argon can maintain depth and precision across multi-step tasks, it was able to coordinate the motions of different elements simultaneously.

Map wildfires and tectonic shockwaves on a 3D globe.

Gemini 4 Argon excels at turning dense, unstructured data into clear visuals. Using Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity, Alex Patrascu (@maxescu on X) combined NASA's live feed of global wildfires and seismic data from the U.S. Geological Survey to create an interactive 3D globe. Argon's frontier reasoning across domains like coding allowed it to parse data, map coordinates, and render animated shockwaves and hotspots.

Engineer an interactive jet engine.

Using Gemini 4 Argon with Blender and Three.js, Ashutosh Shrivastava (@ai_for_success on X) generated a detailed simulation of a high-bypass turbofan jet engine with live measurements and data and part-by-part specs. With enhanced capabilities across coding and the ability to sustain long, multi-step tasks, Argon was able to model individual elements before rendering them together in a 3D environment.

Build a 3D carriage from a single image.

Gemini 4 Argon has the ability to bring flat image files to life. The Bugged Dev (@thebuggeddev on X) gave Argon a single image of a Gothic Victorian carriage and asked it to build the whole thing as an interactive 3D experience. Argon translated the image into a complex rendering with functioning doors and windows, flickering oil lamps, and an undercarriage that reacts to bumps in the road.

Create a multiplayer capture-the-flag game.

Chong-U (@chongdashu on X) used Gemini 4 Argon to build “Backyard Rascals,” a multiplayer browser game where cartoon animals race to capture the other team’s flag. Argon's ability to maintain depth and precision across complex workflows helped this creator build a game with complex features allowing the characters to run, collide, whack each other, and cheer as multiple players engage in real time.

Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra and paid Pro subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
